body.p: Claim(s) 1-20 is/are currently pending in the present application. Claims 1, 8, and 13 has/have been amended by the present amendment in order to place this case in condition for allowance and/or simplify the issues for appeal. Accordingly, entry of the Amendment set forth herein is respectfully requested.
Support for the amendments of claim 1 can be found at least in paragraph [0078] and

FIG. 2D of the instant application. Support for the amendments of claim 8 can be found at least in paragraph [0068] and FIG. 2B of the instant application. Support for the amendments of claim 13 can be found at least in paragraph [0081] and FIG. 2F of the instant application.

The rejection of claim(s) 1-3 and 5-12 under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated over US Patent Application Publication No. US 2014/0303434 to Farritor et al. ("Farritor") is respectfully traversed in part and obviated by amendment in part.

In the Office Action, the Examiner argued, among other things, that Farritor includes "...(e) a shoulder joint comprising: (i) a differential yoke rotationally coupled to the first driveshaft, the differential yoke comprising a yoke body (74) and a yoke lumen therewithin (fig. 2E), wherein the yoke lumen has a longitudinal axis that is transverse to the longitudinal axis of the yoke body..."

Based on the above, is unclear to Applicant what the longitudinal axis is of element 74 (a rotatable pitch housing as described within Farritor) is, what the yoke lumen is, and how any longitudinal axes of each relate to one another. Fig. 2E of Farritor is reproduced below:
However, in order to further prosecution, Applicant has amended each of independent claims 1, 8, and 13 to further distinguish from the cited prior art. Claim 1 now recites:
(e) a shoulder joint comprising:
(i) a differential yoke rotationally coupled to the first driveshaft, the

differential yoke comprising a yoke body and a pair of curved shells extending therefrom and defining a yoke lumen therewithin, wherein the yoke lumen has a longitudinal axis that is transverse to the longitudinal axis of the yoke body, and wherein the differential yoke rotates around a first rotational axis; Element 74 of Farritor as described above does not include "a pair of curved shells extending therefrom and defining a yoke lumen," as amended claim 1 now recites and is described at least in paragraph [0078] and in FIG. 2D of the instant application. Therefore not every limitation of claim 1 as amended is found within Farritor or any other of the cited art.
Claim 8 now recites:
(c) a second driveshaft operably coupled to a second motor, the second
driveshaft coaxial with the first driveshaft and operably coupled at a distal
end to a first bevel gear;

Support for the amendment of claim 8 can be found at least in paragraph [0068] and FIG. 2B of the instant application. Nowhere in Farritor is the second driveshaft coaxial with the first driveshaft. Therefore not every limitation of claim 8 as amended is found within Farritor or any other of the cited art.

For at least these reasons, independent claims 1 and 8 are believed to be patentable over the cited prior art. Similarly, dependent claims 2-7 and 9-12 are believed to be patentable over the prior art as being dependent from an allowable base claim.

The rejection of claim(s) 4 and 13-20 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Farritor in view of US Application Publication No. 2016/0303745 to Rockrohr et al. ("Rockrohr") is respectfully traversed in part and obviated by amendment in part.
While Applicant disagrees with the Examiner's analysis with respect to the obviousness rejection, in order to further prosecution, claim 13 has been amended to include:
(iii) an output body rotatably disposed over the extension shaft and having an
output body gear, the output body gear rotationally coupled to the second
shoulder gear,

Support for the amendments of claim 13 can be found at least in paragraph [0081] and FIG. 2F of the instant application. Neither Farritor nor Rockrohr, either alone or in combination, disclose the output body having an output body gear that is rotationally coupled to the second shoulder gear.

For at least these reasons, in addition to dependent claim 4 being allowable based on the above 102 analysis, independent claim 13 is believed to be patentable over the cited prior art. Similarly, dependent claims 14-20 are believed to be patentable over the prior art as being dependent from an allowable base claim.

While Applicant disagrees with the Examiner's analysis with respect to the rejection, the nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting rejection of claim(s) 1-20 as being unpatentable over claim(s) 1-3 and 6-20 of US Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0303434 to Farritor et al. is obviated by the enclosed terminal disclaimer disclaiming the terminal portion of any patent issuing from the present application which would extend beyond the full statutory term of the '434 publication. In view of the enclosed terminal disclaimer, withdrawal of this ground of rejection is respectfully requested.
In conclusion, and for the foregoing reasons, Applicants submit that this application is in condition for allowance, and early notification to this effect is earnestly solicited.

Applicants believe that the claims are in condition for allowance. A Notice of Allowance for all claims is respectfully requested. If the Examiner has any questions or comments, the Examiner is requested to contact the undersigned at 515-242-8965.
Respectfully submitted, Fredrikson & Byron, P.A.
